title: Can I borrow your charger?
pair_game: Point at a picture. Ask: “Can I borrow your …?” Your partner says yes or no politely. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: Can I …?
grammar_box.tip: Always add please! Can I borrow your pen, **please**?

questions: Can I borrow your pen or pencil?
Do you have a mobile phone?
Can you use a computer well?
Do you play games on your phone or tablet?
Can your friend borrow your book or toy?
What electronic device do you use every day?
Do you ask permission before using things at home?
Can you swim or ride a bike?
Do you have a laptop or tablet at home?
What do you usually do on your phone?

On my phone I usually … and … .
samples: Can I borrow your pen or pencil?
**Yes, of course!** Here you are. But please be **careful** — it is my favourite pen.
What electronic device do you use every day?
I use my phone every day. I use **it** for messages, music and my English app.
Do you ask permission before using things at home?
Yes, I always ask. I say, “**Can I** use the laptop, **please**?” My parents usually say yes.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: What device do you use most?

game.title: Guess my device!
game.rules: Take a card. Do not show it! Read the two sentences. Your group guesses the device.
items: It is small and it is in my pocket. I call my friends with it.
It has a big screen and a keyboard. I write my projects on it.
It is round and small. I put it in my ears.
I use it to take pictures of my family.
It is flat and I read books on it. It has no keyboard.
It is small and black. Without it my phone dies.

mini_talk.title: My devices
plan: Say what you use them for
Say how long you use them
mini_talk.model: At home we have one laptop and I have a small phone. I use my phone every day for messages and music, and I use **it** for my English app too. I use the laptop for my projects. My parents say two hours a day is enough. At school my friend often asks, “**Can I** borrow your charger, **please**?” and I always say, “**Of course!**”
